key_insight: Increasing spanwise convex curvature delays hypersonic boundary-layer transition by weakening centrifugal amplification while preserving the Görtler–sinuous breakdown pathway.
engineering_relevance: Spanwise curvature offers a potential geometry-based approach to delaying transition and managing aerodynamic heating on hypersonic surfaces.
method: Direct numerical simulations and Mach 7 experiments.
Doubly curved surfaces with fixed streamwise concavity and increasing spanwise convex curvature.
Spectral proper orthogonal decomposition to identify dominant disturbance dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations and experiments show consistent trends in transition location, thermal-streak organisation and disturbance evolution, with transition shifting downstream as spanwise curvature increases.
watch_item: Generalisability beyond the studied geometries and Mach 7 conditions remains unestablished; higher-frequency acoustic disturbances become more prominent but remain subdominant.
paper_title: Effects of Spanwise Curvature on Hypersonic Boundary Layer Transition in Görtler-driven Flows
